title: M12 Tangential Flow Filtration
author: Dr. Steven Wilhelm
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.icscawe
materials: Push CAL ZERO and push INTERLOCK OVERRIDE again
Let the washing last for 30-45 min 00:45:00
Again, carefully remove the tubing and pressure sensor.

steps.title: Prepare Cartridge and Initial Connections
steps.instruction: Prepare the cartridge for installation while wearing gloves to protect against acid storage solution.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the M12 is bolted down, preferably near a sink or drain.
Use an arm clamp to hold the cartridge upside-down (the end with only one port).
Connect the sample hosing to this single port.
Connect one pressure sensor to the pressure sensor port using fresh Teflon tape for a secure fit; wait until the cartridge is in its final position before connecting the sensor to the M12.

steps.title: Install Cartridge and Final Hosing
steps.instruction: Position the cartridge upright and connect the remaining lines.

substeps.instruction: Invert the cartridge to the right-side-up position (the end with two ports) and unwrap the parafilm.
Connect the retentate hosing to the horizontally facing port.
Connect the permeate hosing to the vertically facing port, taking care not to break the screw-in connector.
Connect the second pressure sensor to the cartridge and then connect both sensors to the M12 (bottom is inlet, top is outlet).

steps.title: Configure Pump and Tubing
steps.instruction: Set up the pump interface and ensure tubing is correctly positioned.

substeps.instruction: Run the tygon section of the sample hosing through the pump.
Adjust the height and position of the cartridge to eliminate kinks in the hosing.
Close the clamp over the tubing, ensuring the tubing is centered to avoid the round gears chewing through the tygon; use the tubing-covered wire as a buffer.

steps.title: System Priming and Leak Check
steps.instruction: Power on the system and flush the acid storage solution with Milli-Q water.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the M12 power switch (located at the top).
Push the INTERLOCK OVERRIDE button.
Ensure the retentate back pressure valve is fully open (turn counter-clockwise).
Push the START/STOP button to begin the pump at 10% speed and check for leaks.
Increase speed to 15% using the arrows and slowly adjust the retentate valve until inlet and outlet pressures read ~10 each.
Allow 2-4 L of Milli-Q water to run through to flush out the acid storage solution, ensuring the sample hosing does not run dry before turning off the pump and releasing backpressure.

steps.title: Sample Processing
steps.instruction: Filter the sample water using the 30 kDa cartridge.

substeps.instruction: If using natural whole water, pre-filter through GF/F, 0.45 $\mu$m, and 0.2 $\mu$m filters to prevent clogging.
Empty all three hoses of water as much as possible.
Place the sample hosing (marked with a red flag) into the sample container, ensuring the flag is at the bottom to prevent air intake.
Place the retentate hosing end into the sample container.
Place the permeate hosing end into a clean container of similar size to collect the ultrafiltrate.
Turn on the pump and check for proper operation.
Slowly adjust the retentate valve until inlet and outlet pressures read ~15-16; ensure outlet pressure does not exceed 16 or 17.

steps.title: Sample Completion and Rinsing
steps.instruction: Finish the sample run and rinse the system.

substeps.instruction: When the sample level is slightly below the desired limit, turn off the pump and drain hoses into the sample container.
Remove the permeate hosing and drain remaining water into the ultrafiltrate container.
Remove sample water from the M12 (critical for seawater).
Rinse the sample water out with approximately 6 L of Milli-Q or RO water.

steps.title: Cartridge Cleaning
steps.instruction: Wash the cartridge with NaOH to remove contaminants.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1 M NaOH by dissolving NaOH pellets in 1 L RO water in a 2 L beaker.
Place all three hoses into the NaOH beaker and run the solution through the cartridge.
If using the M12 within a day, flush the NaOH with 6 L Milli-Q water.
Otherwise, stop the M12, release backpressure, and let hoses sit in clean water.

steps.title: Cartridge Storage Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the cartridge for long-term storage in acid.

substeps.instruction: Run 4-6 L of water through the system to remove NaOH.
Run 1 L of 0.05 M phosphoric acid through the cartridge (sample hose in acid, retentate/permeate to waste).
Dilute the acid solution 10-fold for final storage.
Once clean water is replaced by the dilute acid solution, turn off the M12 without releasing backpressure or removing hoses.

steps.title: Cartridge Disassembly and Storage
steps.instruction: Disconnect and seal the cartridge for storage at 4ºC.

substeps.instruction: Disconnect pressure sensors from the M12 (keep them connected to the cartridge).
Wearing gloves, disconnect tubing from the top of the cartridge and quickly replace closures.
Wrap closures and the end of the cartridge with a generous amount of parafilm.
Carefully turn the cartridge upside-down, keeping the sample hose end below the top of the acid solution.
Replace the remaining closures and wrap generously with parafilm.
Store the cartridge at 4ºC.
Rinse tubing/hoses with Milli-Q water and dry as much as possible before packing.
Alternatively, place the sample hosing in fresh Milli-Q water and the retentate/permeate hoses in a waste container.
